audio_source_target_position.visual_evidence: The original v1.0.3 Warrior/Bog Moth sequence documented above is visual-only context; neither the video-only stream nor its pixels expose the exact 3D emitter/listener point. No spatial-audio parity is inferred from the footage.
audio_source_target_position.logic_evidence: Original GameObject::GetTargetPosition at 0x3935dc reads its own node pointer +0x180 first. A null node returns actual transform +0x160 even when constructor state initialized optional cache +0x184 to {0,0,0}; only a nonnull node can select the cached point (the original getter also gates it on byte +0x80). Audio callers previously chose cache merely because the std::optional existed. Both RuntimeSessionAudioV1::before_update (player listener anchor) and RuntimeAttackSoundV1::dispatch (step emitter) now use the same feature-local resolver, which checks the actor's own known node token before reading its cache and never follows combat target_id to another actor.
audio_source_target_position.expected_behavior: Known-null or unbound own node uses the actor's current transform; a known nonnull own node with an available cache uses that cached source point. Preserve current actor state/source flags and do not borrow a foreign actor's cache.
audio_source_target_position.uncertainties: ActorState has no separately captured GameObject enabled byte +0x80. The feature-local audio resolver therefore closes the known-null stale-cache bug and selects an available cache for a known nonnull own node, but it does not claim the getter's full disabled-node branch when that byte is unavailable. Unknown/missing cache falls back to current transform.

verification.focused_cases: The audio feature runner invokes the original constructor-prefix helper to create node=0/cache={0,0,0}; asserts the resolver returns actual transform and leaves source_flags520 unchanged; then checks a nonnull own node selects its exact cache and an unbound node ignores a stale zero cache.
